title: Tanzanian Beef Keema
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Nyama ya Kusaga — spiced minced beef with peas, tomatoes, and Tanzanian spices. Fast, affordable, and intensely flavourful — the everyday minced beef dish of urban Tanzania, eaten with chapati, rice, or as a filling for mandazi rolls.
longDesc: Spiced minced beef is the weekday staple of Tanzania's urban households — it cooks in 25 minutes, stretches a small amount of beef to feed a large family, and absorbs the Tanzanian spice palette beautifully.
steps: Add garlic, ginger, and spices. Stir 30 seconds.
Add minced beef. Break apart and brown well — 8 minutes.
chefTips: Brown the mince well — underbrowned mince lacks depth.
Drain excess fat if using fatty mince.
Peas add sweetness and colour — add them last.
commonMistakes: Adding too much water — should be dry, not soupy.
cookingScience: Minced beef provides maximum surface area for Maillard browning — each small piece caramelises independently, producing far more total browned surface than the same weight of whole beef.
sustainabilityTips: Mince uses less premium cuts — a sustainable approach to beef consumption.
healthBenefits: Peas add plant protein and vitamins.
culturalNote: Spiced minced beef is the everyday protein of Tanzania's urban families — the dish that appears when the budget is tight but flavour cannot be compromised.
